scope: Coordination-state model only. Book lifecycle, manuscript identity/version authority, durable persistence backend, routing, dependency-plan semantics, scheduling, retries, cancellation policy, caching and admission remain separate packets/authorities.

terminal_status_rules.COMPLETED_NO_CHANGE: completed_at required; admission_decision_ref may be null; source canonical manuscript remains unchanged.
terminal_status_rules.COMPLETED_ADMITTED: completed_at and admission_decision_ref required; resulting canonical state is referenced by admission evidence outside this workflow state.
terminal_status_rules.FAILED_CLOSED: failed_at required; canonical manuscript effect forbidden.
terminal_status_rules.CANCELLED: cancelled_at required; canonical manuscript effect forbidden.
terminal_status_rules.SUPERSEDED: evidence_receipt_refs must include supersession evidence; no canonical mutation is implied.

binding_rules: Workflow source identity is immutable and must match the exact Book state/manuscript identity used to plan the workflow.
A workflow built against an older Book state or manuscript version must be rejected as stale before further execution or admission handoff.
Workflow state is coordination metadata, not Book lifecycle truth and not canonical manuscript storage.
Raw manuscript/candidate text is prohibited from workflow state; use governed references and hashes.
Context packages and specialist outputs are referenced by immutable identifiers; their schemas are defined by later packets.
A completed-admitted workflow records only the admission decision reference; it does not write resulting canonical state itself.
Retry count is observational coordination state only until Phase 2F/Phase 7 define retry identity and idempotency semantics.
Persistence/recovery guarantees are not claimed until Phase 5 binds this model to durable workflow storage.
